body.text:
The plan is committed as [architecture/DESKTOP.md](architecture/DESKTOP.md) (`3bf4ab0`) — and your branching instinct earned its keep. Rather than reasoning from memory, I drove a scratch repo through the real hooks first. Here's what the evidence says:

**Branching and normal merging survive cleanly, by design.** Every commit on every branch gets its identity; a `--no-ff` merge commit gets its *own* change while the merged-in commits keep theirs. Everything is SHA-anchored, so "which branch" simply never enters the storage model. No design changes needed there.

**But `git merge --squash` is a real, confirmed gap.** The squash commit mints a fresh, *unlinked* change — no fold happens (unlike rebase-squash, which post-rewrite handles) — and the source branch's changes end up anchored to commits that become unreachable once the branch is deleted, meaning GC would eventually leave dangling ledger entries. Since squash-merge is a prominent button in exactly the git clients this app will sit beside, its fix is **step 1 of the build order**: the hook can detect `.git/SQUASH_MSG` at commit time and fold the source changes just like the rebase path, plus a `doctor` audit for already-orphaned history. (Testing also surfaced a subtle rule: our own metadata refs show up in `rev-list --all`, so any branch/graph view must filter them.)

**The app itself** is framed as a *repository intelligence app*, not a git-client replica: v1 adds a repo picker, branch-scoped views, a **diff viewer with the intent beside it** (claim-next-to-evidence extended to the code), and a token-gated actions panel (sync, reindex, annotate, guided repair) — on top of everything the review UI already does, as an Electron shell around the same server and SPA. Deliberately *not* in v1: staging and committing. The build order ships value early — the API groundwork and branch/diff panes work in the plain browser before Electron even exists.

Also recorded: your naming decision (public name TBD, `git-for-ai` internal only) and the npm-publish gate. Three open questions sit at the bottom of the doc — how far "git client" should eventually go, single-window vs per-repo windows, and the naming itself — none blocking the first three build steps. Want me to start on step 1, the squash-merge fold?
Let me first pin down the one mechanical fact the fix hinges on: does `.git/SQUASH_MSG` still exist when the post-commit hook runs, or does git clean it up first?

Fix G1: merge --squash now folds into the surviving change

DESKTOP.md build-order step 1. merge --squash fires no post-rewrite,
so the squash commit previously minted an unlinked fresh change while
the source branch's changes were left on commits that become
unreachable (and gc-doomed) after branch deletion.

Two-phase hook fix, shaped by two empirical facts: SQUASH_MSG exists
at commit-msg time and is deleted before post-commit. commit-msg
detects SQUASH_MSG, parses the squashed commit SHAs, and injects the
SURVIVING change's id (the oldest squashed commit's change, matching
onPostRewrite's first-known-wins rule) as the trailer, writing a
pending-fold file into the git dir. post-commit consumes the file
(always deleted once seen) and folds the other squashed changes via
the ordinary §7.4 onPostRewrite machinery - but only when the
committed trailer matches the recorded survivor id, so a commit
aborted between hooks can never fold a later unrelated commit.
Pre-existing trailers win and skip the fold; squashed commits' own
trailers inside SQUASH_MSG can't interfere (git indents them).

doctor's identity audit gains the unreachable-heads check: change
heads no branch/tag reaches (pre-fix squash-then-delete history) warn
with a relink/tag remediation; metadata refs excluded from
reachability on purpose.

7 new tests (full real-hook squash fold end to end, no-identity
fallback, stale-pending guard, doctor reachability); CLI suite 212
passing. Verified live: the exact scenario that exposed the bug now
yields one continued change with the second absorbed and a clean
doctor. ARCHITECTURE §7.5 and DESKTOP.md G1 updated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
